intro_md:
Written on 29 September 2026. This records the line pass made outside this repository on 28–29 September, in the conversation summarised in `New - Re-plan/Claude Handoff.md` (§3). The author accepted every change, and the chapter now matches the text they supplied.

The chapter as it stood before the pass is saved unchanged as `Drafts/Chapter 3 - The Weight of the Living (Draft 2, before the line pass).md`, and every change here is measured against it. The rounds before the pass are in `Chapter 3 - Changes.md`. **Round 2** (29 September) is change 8, plus edits folded into changes 1 and 6. **Later rounds go on this list** (`Drafts/Chapter 3 - change list (line pass).json`).

Each reason says where it comes from: the handoff when it gives one, or Claude's reading when it doesn't. Changes tagged as the author's own lines replaced something the author wrote or designed; they are listed below, under "The author's own lines this pass replaced".
glance: **"The man" before Silas gives his name:** 8 before the line pass, 10 after it, 9 after round 2 (changes 1 and 2). "The stranger" stays at 2.
summary_md:
## The author's own lines this pass replaced

Changes {tag:authorline}. The handoff records them as accepted. They are listed here because the skill asks that every change to the author's own lines be flagged.

sections.The bridge: The run and the bridge (draft lines 3–57)

changes.title: Silas grounds him
changes.before:
"Stop drowning in self-pity, boy, and move."

Alaric stared at him.

"You want to die? Fine. Stay here and let them have you." He let go. "Then Gerolt died for nothing."
changes.after:
"Move, boy, now, or Gerolt died for nothing!"

He let go and went on.
changes.why: The handoff, §3, lists this as accepted dialogue. It keeps the author's intent ("snap out of it … for Gerolt's sake", "Make Gerolt's death mean he died for nothing") and gives Silas a practical reason to move. It replaces the author's own rough line (Chapter 3 design, line 1: "stop drowning in self-pity … If you want to die, fine, stay"). **Round 2 (29 September):** "The man let go and went on" became "He let go and went on", to bring "the man" back down; he's the only other person there. **Round 2, the line itself (29 September):** Alaric is already standing, so "Get up" went. The author's line: "Move boy, now, or Gerolt died for nothing!" (the comma after "Move" is the house style for calling someone by name, as in Chapter 2's "Get up, boy, or we're both dead!").
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September. The handoff (§3) quotes this line as accepted. Round 2's "He let go": the author, "Agreed". Round 2's line is the author's (29 September).

changes.title: His feet went after the man
changes.before: Alaric didn't know how, and there was no time to ask. He went on, and Alaric's feet went after him.
changes.after: Alaric didn't know how, and there was no time to ask. His feet went after the man.
changes.why: Claude's reading (the handoff gives no reason for this change): follows from change 1, which now says "went on".
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September (the handoff, §3).

changes.title: The river turned him round
changes.before: He went under and came up still holding her. Water filled his mouth and nose. The river turned him round, and the bank went past, and then a fallen tree lying out into the river from the far bank, close enough to touch. He couldn't reach for it without letting go of Wena, so he didn't.
changes.after: He went under and came up still holding her. Water filled his mouth and nose. The river turned him round, the bank went past, and then a fallen tree lying out into the river from the far bank, close enough to touch. He couldn't reach for it without letting go of Wena, so he didn't.
changes.why: The handoff, §3: "The revised river image accepted by the author."
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September. The handoff (§3) quotes this line as accepted.

changes.title: Silas's accusation
changes.before: "And you just sat there looking on like a scared little puppy." He said it quietly. "You did nothing."
changes.after: "And you had his sword in your hands, but you stayed where you were and did nothing," he said quietly.
changes.why: The handoff, §3, lists this as accepted dialogue. It replaces the author's own line from the Chapter 3 design ("like a scared little puppy").
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September. The handoff (§3) quotes this line as accepted.

changes.title: His name, and why Silas was there
changes.before:
He didn't care to ask for Alaric's.

Silas pulled a rag out of the sack and began wiping down his blade. "So how did the old man know you?"
changes.after:
Alaric waited for Silas to ask his name. Instead, Silas pulled a rag out of the sack and began wiping down his blade.

"How did you know Gerolt?"

Silas kept his eyes on the steel. "I heard something from across the river. Sounded like fighting, and by the time I got close enough to see what was happening, it was already too late."

"That isn't what I asked."

"No, it isn't." The rag moved along the blade. "How did you know him?"
changes.why: The handoff, §3: "Chapter 3 was the weakest of the four before its focused revision because Silas withheld both his history and the ordinary reason he had been near the farm. His history should remain hidden; his arrival needed a causal answer." And: "Alaric waits for Silas to ask his name. Silas does not. He begins cleaning his blade instead. This is meant to be observed rather than explained." It replaces "He didn't care to ask for Alaric's" (agreed in round 3), which told the reader what to conclude.
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September. The handoff (§3) quotes this line as accepted.

changes.title: What the scouts were after
changes.before: "Scouts don't come at a farmhouse like that unless something set them off, so what happened back there?"
changes.after: "Scouts don't tear a farmhouse apart unless they're after something, so what happened back there?"
changes.why: Claude's reading (the handoff gives no reason for this change): Silas asks what the scouts wanted rather than what set them off. **Round 2 (29 September):** one sentence again, keeping the line pass's words. On 27 September the author had asked for this line to be one sentence ("make it one sentence").
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September (the handoff, §3). Round 2: the author, "Use the proposed" (29 September).

changes.title: His questions, without the stress
changes.before: *Why me? What did I* do*? And that battle on Gerolt's farm—thousands dead, and he never heard a sound. What* was *that? What's happening to me?*
changes.after: *Why me? What did I do? And that battle on Gerolt's farm—thousands dead, and he never heard a sound. What was that? What's happening to me?*
changes.why: Claude's reading (the handoff gives no reason for this change): the stress on "do" and "was" goes. The handoff (§2): italics are for thought and "rare emphasis carrying genuine stress", not decoration.
changes.decision_note: Accepted in the line pass of 28–29 September (the handoff, §3).

changes.title: I didn't
changes.why: Round 2 (29 September). The line pass changed Silas's question from "So how did the old man know you?" to "How did you know him?", and the answer stayed "He didn't.", which answers the old question. "I didn't" is true: Alaric knew Gerolt for less than a day.
